name: Wharton Global High School Investment Competition
organizer: Wharton Global Youth Program, University of Pennsylvania
prestigeTier: Tier 1 - National/Global flagship
cost: Free (travel to Philadelphia finals not covered)
eligibility: Grades 9-12 worldwide. Teams of 4-6 from the same school + a required teacher advisor. Team leader must be 16+ on day one. Homeschoolers may request approval.
format: 10-week team portfolio simulation (Wharton Investment Simulator) + written deliverables -> semifinal presentations -> Global Finale at Wharton
description: The single best-known investing competition for high schoolers. Each team gets a real Wharton alum as a 'client' with a fictional-but-realistic financial situation, then builds a long-term investment strategy for that client using a $500,000 simulated portfolio (stocks and ETFs only). Crucially, teams are NOT judged on raw returns -- they are judged on the quality and consistency of their strategy versus the client's stated goals and risk tolerance. Deliverables include a team roster, an Investment Policy Statement, and a final report. Roughly 5,400 teams entered the 2025-26 cycle; 49 reached virtual semifinals and 11 made the Global Finale in Philadelphia. Stuyvesant High School won 2026.
timing: 2026-27: Registration opens August 2026. ADVISOR REGISTRATION DEADLINE 5:00pm ET Fri Sept 11, 2026. Competition runs Sept 28 - Dec 4, 2026. Roster due Oct 9, 2026. Finale ~late April 2027.
payoff: Global Finale trip to Wharton, Wharton online course fee waiver for finalists, champion school gets a fast-track semifinal slot next year, strong resume/essay material
notes: THE highest-priority item on this list for your club and the deadline is in ~5 weeks. You need a teacher advisor locked in before Sept 11. Run multiple teams -- there's no cap that hurts you, and it gives more members a real role. The judging-on-strategy-not-returns point is where most teams lose: write the Investment Policy Statement first and make every trade traceable back to it.

name: Young Investors Society (YIS) Global Stock Pitch Competition
prestigeTier: Tier 2 - Strong national, elite within finance circles
eligibility: High school students only, US and international. Solo or teams of up to 2. Teammates may be from different schools but must register under the same state event.
format: Submit a written stock pitch report + PowerPoint + YouTube video of your presentation -> state/territory judging -> top 100 invited to NYC quarterfinals -> semis (24) -> finals (5)
description: The closest thing to a genuine professional equity research experience available at the high school level. Students pick one publicly traded company, do real fundamental research (some teams even get calls with company investor relations or management), build an intrinsic value model, and issue a Buy or Sell recommendation. All three components -- report, deck, and video -- are required. Winners advance to the Global Youth Investment Summit in New York City, a two-day event with workshops, industry speakers, case competitions, and networking. YIS also publishes free templates, an intrinsic value model, a Stock Investing 101 eBook, and past winning pitches on YouTube.
timing: 2025-26 cycle: registration opened Dec 12, closed Feb 20; NYC Summit May 28-29. Expect a near-identical 2026-27 calendar -- watch for December registration.
payoff: NYC Global Youth Investment Summit invite, industry networking, a portfolio-quality work product you can show any admissions officer or future employer
notes: Highest skill ceiling per dollar on this list. The written pitch is a genuinely reusable artifact -- students can put the PDF in a portfolio. Note NYC travel is family-funded; start fundraising in the fall if you want to send teams.

name: YIS Finance Knowledge Bowl
prestigeTier: Tier 3 - Solid skill-builder
cost: Low / free for chapters (confirm current cycle)
commitment: Light -- study sessions plus event day
eligibility: High school students, generally through YIS chapters
format: Quiz-bowl style rapid-fire finance and investing questions
description: A team trivia-style competition on investing and finance fundamentals -- terminology, market mechanics, valuation basics, financial history. Lower barrier than the Stock Pitch Competition and a good way to get newer or younger club members competing early, and to build the shared vocabulary the rest of your club activities depend on.
timing: Runs during the school year; check the MyYIS calendar
payoff: Recognition, team-building, foundational knowledge
notes: Excellent onboarding activity for freshmen and sophomores. Use it as your club's fall recruiting hook.
confidence: Verified page exists Aug 2026 -- confirm 2026-27 dates/fees with YIS

name: YIS CYIA (Certified Young Investment Analyst) Designation
prestigeTier: Tier 3 - Niche but concrete
eligibility: High school students
format: Self-paced coursework and assessment leading to a designation
description: A structured, credential-bearing curriculum for high schoolers that mirrors -- at an introductory level -- the logic of professional designations like the CFA. Useful as a concrete, verifiable line on a resume that shows sustained study rather than one-off participation.
timing: Self-paced
payoff: A named designation and a defensible knowledge base
notes: Good club-wide goal: 'every member earns CYIA by spring.' Creates a measurable club outcome you can report to your school.

name: The Stock Market Game (SMG)
prestigeTier: Tier 3 - Broad participation, low selectivity
cost: Free in most states (sponsor-funded); NC funded via NCCEE sponsors
eligibility: Grades 4-12, US. Team-based, run through a teacher/advisor. Available in NC through the NC Council on Economic Education.
format: Online portfolio simulation, $100,000 hypothetical, real-time pricing, stocks/bonds/ETFs/mutual funds
description: The oldest and most widely used investing simulation in American schools -- nearly 20 million students since 1977. Teams manage a hypothetical $100,000 portfolio against real market data and compete on portfolio performance within their state and grade division. Lower analytical rigor than the research-and-pitch competitions, but it is free, easy to run, has excellent teacher support materials, and works as a semester-long backbone activity that everyone in a club can participate in simultaneously.
timing: Fall and spring sessions plus a year-long option; register through NCCEE
payoff: State/regional recognition, awards banquets, hands-on market familiarity
notes: Use this as your club's 'everyone plays' baseline activity while your strongest teams do Wharton and YIS. It also unlocks InvestWrite eligibility.

name: InvestWrite
prestigeTier: Tier 3 - Good national recognition, modest selectivity
eligibility: Grades 4-12 -- but ONLY open to students participating in The Stock Market Game
format: National essay competition responding to an annual prompt; advisors submit the best essays
description: The written companion to the Stock Market Game. Students write an essay applying investing concepts -- long-term strategy, diversification, risk -- to a prompt set each session. Essays are scored on rationale, subject-matter understanding, and writing style by volunteer industry judges. It rewards students who can explain their reasoning, which is a different and often rarer skill than picking stocks.
timing: Fall and spring deadlines tied to SMG sessions
payoff: National and state recognition, awards ceremonies, judged by finance professionals
notes: Cheap add-on: if you're already running SMG, entering InvestWrite costs you nothing extra and doubles the recognition surface. Good for members who write well but aren't quant-oriented.

name: Capitol Hill Challenge
organizer: SIFMA Foundation, presented by the Charles Schwab Foundation
prestigeTier: Tier 2 - Prestigious but access-limited
eligibility: INVITATION ONLY. Public middle and high schools, priority to Title I schools with highest need. Up to 2 schools per Member of Congress, up to 15 teams per school, 3-5 students per team.
format: Special edition of the Stock Market Game; each team is paired with your local Member of Congress
description: A national version of the Stock Market Game that reaches every US Congressional district, pairing student teams with their Representative or Senator. Top-10 teams nationally earn recognition and the opportunity to meet with government officials in Washington. The 2026 edition ran Jan 26 - May 1 with a June celebration. Rules include a $5-per-trade commission, so it rewards discipline rather than churn.
timing: Roughly late January - early May; roster deadline was March 6 in 2026
payoff: National top-10 recognition, meetings with Members of Congress, DC celebration
notes: You cannot simply apply -- you have to be invited. If your school is public and Title I eligible, have your advisor email capitolhill@sifma.org to express interest. Otherwise treat this as aspirational.

name: NC Capitol Challenge (Stock Market Game)
organizer: North Carolina Council on Economic Education (NCCEE), Raleigh
prestigeTier: Tier 3 - Strong state-level visibility
eligibility: North Carolina middle and high school teams
format: Statewide Stock Market Game variant pairing student teams with NC General Assembly members
description: North Carolina's own version of the Capitol Hill Challenge. Student teams across the state are paired with members of the NC General Assembly and compete on portfolio growth. Sponsored at the high school level by State Farm, with credit union and Fidelity support. A genuinely local way to get your club in front of state legislators -- which is unusual access for a high school investing club and makes for excellent local press.
timing: Runs during the school year; contact NCCEE for the 2026-27 window
payoff: Recognition at regional awards banquets, contact with state legislators
notes: NCCEE is headquartered right in Raleigh (8380 Six Forks Road). Get your advisor on their mailing list -- they run the state qualifiers for the national Econ and Personal Finance Challenges too. This is your single highest-leverage local relationship.

name: CME Group Trading Challenge (monthly)
prestigeTier: Tier 4 for HS (prize-ineligible) but excellent learning
eligibility: Open registration but AGE-RESTRICTED for prizes -- terms specify age limits and eligible countries. Most high schoolers under 18 will be practice-only.
format: One-week futures trading simulation on a professional platform, plus required CME Institute coursework
description: A recurring (roughly monthly) simulated futures trading competition. Participants trade CME products -- equity index, energy, metals, agricultural futures, including micro contracts -- in a live-market simulator, with cash prizes for top leaderboard finishers and daily P&L winners. Requires completing CME Institute courses to qualify for prizes. Even where students are ineligible for prizes, the free CME Institute curriculum on futures and derivatives is genuinely good and hard to find elsewhere at this level.
timing: Recurring monthly windows; e.g. Aug 9-14, 2026
payoff: Free derivatives education; cash prizes only for eligible (adult) participants
notes: READ THE TERMS before your members register -- age restrictions vary by cycle. Use it as a club learning module on derivatives rather than a credential. Nothing else free teaches futures this well.
confidence: Verified Aug 2026 -- confirm age terms each cycle

name: IMC Prosperity (algorithmic trading challenge)
prestigeTier: Practice-only for HS; Tier 1 in the quant world
eligibility: Platform open to anyone for learning. Prizes and leaderboard ranking restricted to university students 18+. High schoolers can play but cannot win.
format: Two-week Python-based algorithmic + manual trading simulation across five rounds
description: A large, well-run global trading challenge where teams write Python trading algorithms to compete in a simulated market covering market making, options, and risk. Over 48,000 players have participated across editions. High school students can sign up and play for learning purposes -- and this is one of the best available introductions to quantitative trading -- but only 18+ university students are eligible for the $50,000 prize pool and official ranking.
timing: Registration opens ~mid-March, competition mid-to-late April
payoff: Real algorithmic trading experience, active Discord community, Python portfolio work
notes: Be honest with members: they cannot win. But for anyone considering quant, this plus AMC/AIME is the real pipeline. A club 'quant track' could do the tutorial round together in the spring.

name: Ascend Berkeley Stock Pitch Competition
prestigeTier: Commercial - low admissions signal, decent practice
cost: $45-$55 per student depending on deadline tier
eligibility: Teams of 2-5, all from the same school. Separate middle school and high school categories.
format: Preliminary pitch deck submission -> top 8 per category present live on Zoom to judges
description: A paid pitch-deck competition with a high school track focused on stock picking toward a defined investment goal. Finalists present live to a judging panel of professors and industry experts. Legitimate as practice and feedback, but understand what you are buying: entry fees run $45-$55 per student and the organizer is a for-profit education company, not the university itself.
timing: Priority deadline ~mid-November, regular ~early December, late ~early January
payoff: Judge feedback, certificates, live presentation practice
notes: Skip this if budget is tight -- YIS gives you more for $25. Included here so you can recognize the category: many 'university-branded' high school competitions are run by third-party companies. Always check who actually operates the event.

name: Regional / local stock pitch competitions (e.g. Wall Street South, Stevens Trading Day)
organizer: Regional economic development boards, universities, local finance firms
prestigeTier: Tier 3 regionally, but exceptional networking value
eligibility: Varies -- usually restricted to schools in a defined region
format: Live pitch competitions judged by local finance executives
description: A fast-growing category worth tracking. The inaugural Wall Street South Stock Pitch Competition (Palm Beach County, Jan 2026) brought 21 high schools to pitch live to 15 finance executives including the Head of Florida for Point72, with a traveling trophy and career talks. Stevens Institute runs a Trading Day for high school sophomores and juniors using StockTrak. These events offer something national competitions cannot: direct, in-person contact with working professionals who hire.
timing: Varies by region
payoff: Face time with local finance professionals, internship leads, local press
notes: ACTION ITEM: nothing like this exists in the Triangle yet as far as I found. Given Fidelity's large RTP campus, Raleigh's banking presence, and NCCEE being local, your club could credibly propose founding one. That would be a far stronger leadership story than winning any single competition.

name: National Economics Challenge (NEC)
organizer: Council for Economic Education (CEE); NC state round run by NCCEE
prestigeTier: Tier 1 - National flagship
eligibility: Teams of 3-4 high school students enrolled for HS credit during the academic year. Two divisions: Adam Smith (AP/IB/honors and returning competitors) and David Ricardo (first-timers with no more than one econ course).
format: Online state qualifying exams -> state finals -> online national semifinals -> in-person national finals
description: America's premier high school economics competition, and it is genuinely hard. Content covers microeconomics, macroeconomics, international economics, and current events. The national semifinal is a 45-question multiple-choice exam; the finals add a critical thinking/case round and a rapid-fire quiz bowl where teams answer in about 20 seconds per question. The two-division structure is the key strategic feature -- David Ricardo gives beginners a real shot without facing AP veterans.
timing: 2026 cycle: state exams Jan-Mar, online semifinals Apr 20-24, national finals Atlanta May 27-29. Expect a similar 2027 calendar; NC registration through NCCEE opens in winter.
payoff: Cash prizes ($1,000 / $500 / $250 / $200 per team member plus coach), national recognition, CNBC coverage
notes: Enter BOTH divisions if you have the members -- Ricardo is a realistic medal shot for underclassmen while Smith develops your AP Econ students. Pair with AP Macro/Micro coursework so the studying does double duty.

name: NC EconChallenge (state round of the NEC)
organizer: North Carolina Council on Economic Education
prestigeTier: Tier 2 - Gateway to Tier 1
eligibility: NC high school teams; top 8 per division (max 2 teams per school) advance to state championship
format: Online qualifying exam -> NC Live State Championship -> national semifinals
description: North Carolina's qualifying pathway to the National Economics Challenge. Top eight scoring teams per division from the online round are invited to the live state championship. Winners advance to the national semifinals. Because it runs through NCCEE in Raleigh, this is one of the most locally accessible high-prestige competitions available to you.
timing: Online testing window in winter/spring; watch NCCEE for 2026-27 dates
payoff: State championship title, path to nationals
notes: Note the 'no more than two teams per school' cap at the state championship level -- pick your strongest two rosters rather than diluting across many.

name: High School Fed Challenge
organizer: Federal Reserve System (administered by the NY Fed, with Dallas and Richmond)
prestigeTier: Tier 2 - Federal Reserve imprimatur, genuine publication
eligibility: Grades 9-12 at any high school in one of the 12 Federal Reserve Districts. No prior economics coursework required. Team-based with a faculty advisor.
format: Research and writing competition -- teams write an economics podcast script on an annual theme
description: Now in its 31st year, this is a research-and-writing competition rather than a live debate. Each year the Fed announces a theme (2025-26 was 'Economics of Music') and teams write a podcast script analyzing any topic connected to it. Reviewers select the best submissions for publication in the Journal of Future Economists. In 2026, 207 papers were submitted and 12 were selected for publication. All participating schools receive recognition in the Journal. The creative-theme format makes it unusually accessible to students who haven't taken economics.
timing: 2025-26 cycle: theme announced Sept 9, registration deadline Feb 17, papers due Mar 16, decisions May 15. Expect a similar 2026-27 calendar with a September theme announcement.
payoff: Publication in the Journal of Future Economists, certificates for all participants, Federal Reserve recognition
notes: 'Published by the Federal Reserve' is a rare and durable line for a 17-year-old. The creative theme means strong writers can beat stronger economists. Watch for the September 2026 theme announcement.

name: USA Economics and Business Olympiad (USAEBO) -> International Economics Olympiad (IEO)
prestigeTier: Tier 1 - International olympiad, top-tier admissions signal
cost: Registration fee for USAEBO (modest); IEO travel covered/organized for Team USA
eligibility: Individual. Under 20 as of June 30 of the Olympiad year, HS graduation date after Dec 1 of the prior year. For Team USA: US citizen, permanent resident, or full-time US middle/high school student.
format: Round 1 open multiple-choice exam -> Round 2 final round -> 5 students selected for Team USA -> IEO (economics/finance MCQ, open questions, and a business case presented to an international jury)
description: The most academically demanding option on this list and the only true international olympiad in economics. USAEBO is the sole pathway onto Team USA. At the IEO itself, contestants sit an economics and finance multiple-choice exam, answer open-ended questions, and present a business case to an international jury. In 2026 the IEO was held July 12-19 in Shenzhen, China, with 52 national teams; it was the first year the US competed in person and Team USA placed 6th. Over 74 countries have participated historically.
timing: USAEBO registration typically opens in winter; IEO each July
payoff: Team USA selection, international medals, elite recognition
notes: Individual, not team, so it's a personal-glory track rather than a club activity -- but sponsor your strongest econ student into it. NAMING WARNING: several unrelated organizations use similar names ('International Economics Olympiad' at econolympiad.org, 'Economics Olympiad' at economicsolympiad.org). The official IEO is ieo-official.org and the only US pathway is usaebo.org. Verify before paying anyone.

name: Economics Olympiad (EO) Americas Challenge
prestigeTier: Tier 2/3 - Real but less established in the US
eligibility: High school students aged roughly 14-20 in North and South America
format: School Round online exam -> Intercontinental Round in person -> International Finals
description: A separate international economics competition from the IEO, structured as School, Regional, National, and International rounds. The 2026 Americas Challenge ran a School Round online in late February, invited the top 100 students to an in-person Intercontinental Round at Universidad Francisco Marroquin in Guatemala City in May, and sent the top 10 to International Finals in August. Legitimate, but distinct from and less established in the US than USAEBO/IEO.
timing: School Round late February; later rounds spring/summer
payoff: International travel rounds, recognition
notes: Don't confuse this with the IEO. If a student is choosing one, USAEBO/IEO carries more weight in the US. This is a reasonable second shot.

name: National Personal Finance Challenge (NPFC)
organizer: Council for Economic Education, with the Voya Foundation; NC round via NCCEE
prestigeTier: Tier 1 - National flagship in personal finance
eligibility: Teams of 3-4 high school students, must have a coach affiliated with the school. Students represent the state they're enrolled in.
format: Online 30-question qualifying round -> state finals -> in-person national finals (case study financial plan + quiz bowl for the top 16)
description: The national counterpart to the Economics Challenge, focused on practical money management: earning, spending, saving, investing, credit, insurance, and risk. The national finals require teams to build a complete financial plan for a fictitious family and present it to judges, then the top 16 advance to a quiz bowl. CEE covers lodging and group meals for national finalists (transportation excluded). 38 teams reached the 2026 finals in Atlanta on June 1.
timing: 2026 cycle: state rounds through the school year, advancement notifications by Apr 28, national finals Atlanta May 31 - Jun 1. NC round ran Jan 20 - Mar 28, 2026 via NCCEE.
payoff: All-expenses-covered national finals (excl. travel), national championship title, cash prizes
notes: Materially easier than the Economics Challenge but nearly as recognized, so the effort-to-reward ratio is excellent. North Carolina now requires a standalone personal finance course to graduate, which means your members are already studying the content. The NC state championship was hosted at Fidelity's Durham campus in 2026 -- that is a networking room worth being in.

name: NC Personal Finance Challenge
organizer: North Carolina Council on Economic Education
prestigeTier: Tier 2 - Direct path to nationals, strong local visibility
eligibility: NC middle and high school students; high school teams compete toward the state championship and then nationals
format: Online multiple-choice exam -> state championship (written assessment, 48-hour family case study, quiz bowl)
description: North Carolina's qualifier for the NPFC. The state championship has three phases: an individual timed written assessment aggregated into a team score, a detailed fictitious family scenario with 48 hours to prepare a financial plan presented to expert judges, and a quiz bowl for the top two teams per division. The 2026 championship was held at Fidelity Investments in Durham, with the State Treasurer in attendance.

payoff: State championship, national qualification, exposure to Fidelity and state officials
notes: Realistically your club's most winnable high-visibility state title. Contact Amber Thomas at NCCEE (acthomas@nccee.org, 919-791-1995) before the fall to get on the list early.

name: Knowledge Matters Virtual Business Challenge (VBC)
organizer: Knowledge Matters, run in partnership with DECA
prestigeTier: Tier 3 - Solid, DECA-linked
cost: Included with DECA participation (chapter fees apply)
eligibility: High school DECA chapter members
format: Online business simulation across eight tracks including Personal Finance, Accounting, and Entrepreneurship; two qualifying rounds then live competition at ICDC
description: A set of online business simulations where students run a virtual business or manage virtual personal finances, scored competitively. Eight tracks are available to DECA members. Two internet-based qualifying rounds run during the school year, with live timed sessions in the exhibit hall at DECA's International Career Development Conference. Scholarships awarded to the top three at ICDC.

name: DECA (finance and entrepreneurship competitive events)
prestigeTier: Tier 2 - Widely recognized, ICDC placement is a real credential
cost: Membership dues plus conference registration and travel (can be several hundred dollars per student)
commitment: Sustained -- fall prep through spring conferences
eligibility: Members of a chartered high school DECA chapter (~224,000 HS members)
format: District -> state (association) -> International Career Development Conference (ICDC). Role-plays and case studies, prepared written events, and online simulations.
description: The largest business-focused competitive organization for high schoolers, with roughly 60 event options across marketing, finance, hospitality, management, entrepreneurship, and personal financial literacy. Finance-relevant events include Personal Financial Literacy, Financial Consulting, Accounting Applications, Business Finance Series, Financial Literacy Project, Financial Services Team Decision Making, and the DECA Stock Market Game. Role-play events give students 10-15 minutes to solve a case in front of a judge; prepared events require a written project plus presentation and must be started early in the fall.
timing: Year-round. 2026-27 ICDC prepared-event submissions open in late March 2027.
payoff: ICDC medals, scholarships, networking with 80+ corporate and university partners
notes: If your school has a DECA chapter, your investing club should feed it -- the finance cluster events are the natural competitive outlet. If it doesn't, starting one is a legitimate club project. Budget matters: conference costs are the real barrier, so plan fundraising early.

name: FBLA (Securities & Investments and finance events)
prestigeTier: Tier 2 - Well recognized, national placement carries weight
cost: Dues plus conference registration and travel
commitment: Study through the year, conferences in spring/summer
eligibility: Members of a chartered high school FBLA chapter, grades 9-12; dues typically due by December 1
format: Chapter/region -> State Leadership Conference -> National Leadership Conference. Objective tests, role plays, and presentation events.
description: FBLA runs 70+ competitive events. The accounting and finance cluster includes Securities & Investments (an objective test covering investment fundamentals, stocks, bonds, mutual funds, derivatives, portfolio management, risk analysis, and financial services regulation), Accounting I and II, Banking & Financial Systems (test plus role play), and Personal Finance. Placing top 10 at nationals makes you ineligible to re-enter that event, which pushes students to broaden. The NLC draws roughly 12,000-15,000 attendees.
timing: 2026-27 competitive event guidelines post in early September 2026. NLC 2027: Columbus, OH, June 23-26.
payoff: National placement, scholarships, employer and university judging exposure
notes: Securities & Investments is the most directly relevant event to an investing club and it's a pure objective test -- which means it is highly coachable. Build a study group around it; that alone can justify weekly club meetings.

name: Business Professionals of America (BPA) - Finance events
prestigeTier: Tier 3 - Less prestigious than DECA/FBLA, better odds
cost: Dues plus conference costs; virtual events much cheaper
eligibility: Members of a chartered BPA chapter; membership deadline March 15
format: Regional -> State -> National Leadership Conference. Also national-only Virtual Competitions requiring no regional/state qualification.
description: A third CTSO with a Workplace Skills Assessment Program organized into six areas including Finance. Smaller than DECA and FBLA, which cuts both ways -- less prestige, but meaningfully better odds of placing. Notably, BPA offers Virtual Competitions available at the national level only, open to all student members with no qualifying rounds, specifically designed for students whose schools can't fund travel.
timing: Regionals in winter, state in early spring, NLC in May
payoff: National placement, workplace skills credentials
notes: The virtual-only national competitions are underrated if travel budget is your constraint -- a genuine national placement without a plane ticket.

name: Modeling the Future Challenge (MTFC)
organizer: The Actuarial Foundation, with the Institute of Competition Sciences
prestigeTier: Tier 2 - Highly respected, genuinely rigorous
eligibility: High school students; individual or teams of up to 5
format: Scenario Phase (dataset + up to 30 questions) -> Semifinalists advance to Project Phase (original actuarial research project) -> regional -> national finals
description: A risk-analysis and actuarial modeling competition that is far more rigorous than most business competitions. Teams first work through a structured scenario with a provided dataset, then semifinalists conduct their own original research project modeling real-world data to analyze risks and make recommendations to a company, industry group, or government. About $60,000 in scholarship prizes. 593 students participated in 2025-26. Free training webinars and Excel training materials are provided.
timing: Registration reopens August 2026 for the 2026-27 season
payoff: Up to $60,000 in scholarship prizes, real research experience, actuarial career pathway
notes: Registration is opening RIGHT NOW. This is the best option on the list for a mathematically strong member who wants to produce original research rather than analysis of someone else's prompt. Also the clearest on-ramp to actuarial science, which is an underrated finance career.

name: MathWorks Math Modeling (M3) Challenge
organizer: SIAM (Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics), sponsored by MathWorks
prestigeTier: Tier 1 - Top-tier quantitative credential
eligibility: US high school juniors and seniors (incl. territories and DoDEA), plus sixth form students in England and Wales. Teams of 3-5 with a teacher coach. Max two teams per school. Homeschool/cyber school eligible. Under 18 needs parental consent.
format: Teams choose any 14-hour window during Challenge weekend to solve an unseen real-world problem and submit a written paper
description: A 14-hour intensive applied math modeling sprint. The problem is unknown until teams log in on Challenge weekend, and it is always a genuine open-ended real-world question -- past topics have covered remote work impacts, the digital divide, and extreme heat. Papers are judged by PhD applied mathematicians in three phases, with triage eliminating two-thirds or more. Over $100,000 in scholarship awards annually and nearly 80,000 students served over two decades.
timing: 2026 cycle: registration deadline Feb 20, Challenge weekend Feb 27 - Mar 2. Expect similar 2027 dates.
payoff: Over $100,000 in scholarships, national media coverage for top teams
notes: Not finance-specific, but modeling and data skills are exactly what quant finance recruits on -- and it is free with real scholarship money. The two-team-per-school cap means you should choose rosters deliberately. Practice on past problems in January.

name: AMC 10/12 -> AIME -> USAMO (quant finance pipeline)
organizer: Mathematical Association of America; prizes sponsored by Jane Street, Citadel/Citadel Securities, and Two Sigma
prestigeTier: Tier 1 for quant pathways
cost: Small exam fee, usually covered by the school
eligibility: AMC 10 for grade 10 and below, AMC 12 for grade 12 and below; taken at school or an approved site
format: Multiple-choice exams -> AIME qualification -> USAMO/USAJMO
description: Not a finance competition, but included deliberately: the top quantitative trading firms literally sponsor these exams (Jane Street sponsors the AMC 12 prizes, Citadel Securities the AMC 10 A, Two Sigma the AMC 10 B). AIME qualification is the most reliable single signal a high schooler can produce for quant trading and research recruiting later on. If any of your members are aiming at Jane Street, Citadel, Optiver, or SIG, this matters more than any investing competition on this list.
timing: AMC 10/12 A and B in November, AIME in February
payoff: AIME/USAMO qualification, direct recruiting visibility with quant firms
notes: Worth saying out loud at a club meeting: students who want quant should treat math contests as the main event and investing competitions as the supplement. Students who want investment banking, asset management, or corporate finance should do the reverse.

name: John Locke Institute Global Essay Prize - Economics category
prestigeTier: Tier 1 - Internationally prestigious

name: Marshall Society Essay Competition
organizer: The Marshall Society, University of Cambridge
prestigeTier: Tier 2 - Strong academic signal, Cambridge affiliation
eligibility: Any student who has not yet begun university studies, worldwide
format: Single economics essay on one of several set prompts
description: Run by Cambridge's undergraduate economics society. name: Diamond Challenge

Two tracks: Business Innovation (revenue and market focused) and Social Innovation (impact driven). Over $100,000 in prizes, with grand prizes around $12,000 / $8,000 / $4,500 per track plus topical awards in areas like waste and recycling innovation and technology application.
